==English==
{{wp}}

===Alternative forms===
* {{alt|en|individuall||obsolete}}

===Etymology===
{{PIE word|en|dwóh₁}}
From {{der|en|la-med|indīviduālis}}, from {{der|en|la|indīviduum|t=an indivisible thing}}, neuter of {{m|la|indīviduus|t=indivisible, undivided}}, from {{m|la|in}} + {{m|la|dīviduus|t=divisible}}, from {{m|la|dīvidō|t=divide}}. Displaced native {{noncog|ang|hād||person, individual}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{a|en|RP}}
** {{IPA|en|/ɪndɪˈvɪd͡ʒʊəl/|/ɪndɪˈvɪd͡ʒʊl/|a=yod-coalescence}}
** {{IPA|en|/ɪndɪˈvɪdjʊəl/|/ɪndɪˈvɪdjʊl/|a=no <<yod-coalescence>>}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˌɪndɪˈvɪd͡ʒ(u)əl/|/ˌɪndə-/|a=GA}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-individual.ogg|a=US}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# A [[person]] considered alone, rather than as belonging to a [[group]] of [[people]].
#: {{ux|en|He is an unusual '''individual'''.}}
#* {{RQ:NYT|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2024/09/16/dining/drinks/customized-drinks.html|passage=“You have to be an '''individual''',” said Ms. Smoke, a 40-year-old saleswoman, as she sipped her beverage. “You can’t just get black coffee.”|author=Priya Krishna|date=Sept. 16, 2024|title=The Customized Drink Is Out of Control|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20240919224319/https://www.nytimes.com/2024/09/16/dining/drinks/customized-drinks.html}}
# {{lb|en|legal}} A single physical [[human being]] as a legal subject, as opposed to a [[legal person]] such as a [[corporation]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1982|title=Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms
|passage=Every '''individual''' is equal before and under the law and has the right to the equal protection and equal benefit of the law without discrimination […].}}
# An [[object]], be it a thing or an agent, as contrasted to a [[class]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2006|chapter=Identity and Individuality in Quantum Theory|title=Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy|author=Steven French|url=http://plato.stanford.edu/entries/qt-idind/
|passage=It is typically held that chairs, trees, rocks, people and many of the so-called ‘everyday’ objects we encounter can be regarded as '''individuals'''.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=2013|month=May-June|author=[http://www.americanscientist.org/authors/detail/katrina-g-claw Katrina G. Claw]
|title=[http://www.americanscientist.org/issues/feature/2013/3/rapid-evolution-in-eggs-and-sperm Rapid Evolution in Eggs and Sperm]
|volume=101|issue=3|magazine=w:American Scientist
|passage=In plants, the ability to recognize self from nonself plays an important role in fertilization, because self-fertilization will result in less diverse offspring than fertilization with pollen from another '''individual'''.}}
# {{lb|en|statistics}} An element belonging to a population.

===Adjective===
{{en-adj}}

# Relating to a single [[person]] or [[thing]] as opposed to more than one.
#: {{syn|en|single#Adjective}}
#: {{ant|en|collective#Adjective}}
#: {{nearsyn|en|individuated|solitary#Adjective|self-standing|freestanding}}
#: {{ux|en|As we can't print them all together, the '''individual''' pages will have to be printed one by one.}}
#* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-06-01|volume=407|issue=8838|page=71
|title=[http://www.economist.com/news/finance-and-economics/21578670-peer-peer-lending-needs-new-name-end-peer-show End of the peer show]
|passage=Finance is seldom romantic. But the idea of peer-to-peer lending comes close. This is an industry that brings together '''individual''' savers and lenders on online platforms. Those that want to borrow are matched with those that want to lend.}}
# Intended for a single [[person]] as opposed to more than one person.
#: {{syn|en|personal#Adjective|single#Adjective}}
#: {{ant|en|group#Noun<!--in attributive position (noun adjunct)-->|joint#Adjective|shared#Adjective|collective#Adjective}}
#: {{coi|en|'''individual''' personal pension}};   {{coi|en|'''individual''' cream cakes}}
# Not [[divisible]] without losing its [[identity]].
#: {{nearsyn|en|unatomizable|indivisible|undividable}}
